messages:
jordan_support: forwarding a customer report from Acme — their rerank calls suddenly return a 413. customer says it started after adding older docs to the corpus. copying the error they sent below.

acme_dev: 
HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "input_limit_exceeded",
  "message": "token ceiling exceeded",
  "details": { "got_tokens": 45216, "max_tokens": 32768, "doc_count": 5600 }
}

jordan_support: repro attempt from my machine — customer sends query + ~5.6k short docs (~120–250 words each). request body ~5.2MB. we get the 413 almost immediately. sending smaller doc set works. attaching curl they used below.

acme_dev: curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{
    "query": "What is the onboarding flow?",
    "documents": [ ... 5600 items ... ]
  }'

sam_support: quick notes: customer expects either clearer guidance or a different error. they said the error just said "payload too large" with no hint which field to change. asked for recommended client-side mitigations.

kai_engineer: quick triage — this is expected behavior: our rerank input token budget counts tokenized(query) + sum(tokenized(doc) + delimiter) for each doc. the limit is enforced before early truncation because we need full doc tokens to compute scores. a few things to call out:
- their doc_count * average tokens ~= 45k tokens -> over 32k limit.
- we don't currently include token counts in the error response for privacy reasons, but internal logs have the breakdown.

kai_engineer: repro steps I ran:
```bash
# synthetic repro: create 5k docs of ~200 words and POST
python tools/make_docs.py --count 5600 --avg-words 180 > docs.json
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H "Authorization: Bearer X" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @payload_big.json -w "HTTPSTATUS:%{http_code}\n"
# server returns 413 with no token metadata in body
```

kai_engineer: internal log line: 
```
level=warn service=rerank request_id=rid_01 tokens_total=45216 tokens_limit=32768 docs=5600 query_tokens=28 largest_doc_tokens=3200
```

maria_prod: product ask: can we make the error actionable? suggestion: return a structured error with fields: 
- reason: "token_limit"
- got_tokens: int
- max_tokens: int
- doc_count: int
- suggestion: string (e.g., "truncate documents or pass snippets")
This would let support and customers show tailored guidance without guessing.

kai_engineer: implementation note: we can add those fields to the 413 body. we avoid returning full tokenized content, but returning counts and doc_count is safe. also we could include a sample_doc_index that contributed most to tokens (index only) to help customers find large docs. minimal API change.

sam_support: +1 from support. customers keep hitting this when they bulk-upload archives. typical recommended fixes we give:
- send only top-k candidate docs for rerank (pre-filter by embedding similarity)
- truncate long docs to first N tokens or pass a summary field
- chunk docs into passages and score the top passages rather than every doc
Add a short example snippet to KB.

jordan_support: suggested KB snippet for customers:
```
# example: client-side prefiltering using embeddings (python pseudo)
query_emb = embed(query)
docs_embs = embed_batch(docs)
scores = cosine(query_emb, docs_embs)
# pick top 200 docs by score before calling /rerank
candidates = select_top(docs, scores, k=200)
# call rerank with candidates only
resp = client.rerank(query, candidates)
```

maria_prod: also product question — should we offer an optional server-side auto-truncate flag like `allow_truncate=true` that truncates docs to max per-doc tokens and proceeds (with a warning)? pros/cons?

kai_engineer: pros: fewer support tickets. cons: truncation can change scores and affect ranking quality; dangerous for legal/regulatory customers who expect full-doc scoring. If we add it, default must be off and only available to hosted non-enterprise or with explicit consent.

sam_support: customer follow-up asked whether there's an easy way to estimate token usage before hitting the API. can we add a lightweight endpoint `POST /v1/estimate_tokens` that returns token_estimate for query+docs? would be useful in SDKs.

kai_engineer: we can add a local estimator in SDKs (tokenizer port) and a server endpoint that does a fast pass (no heavy scoring) to return counts. low overhead. ops-bot: created ticket INT-5234 to track adding token metadata to 413 body and SDK estimator.

ops-bot: INT-5234 created: components=[rerank, api], priority=P2, owner=kai_engineer

jordan_support: action items for us:
- tell acme to prefilter to top-200 docs and try again (we provided sample code) — sam, can you ping them with that?
- engineering to add token fields to 413 response and SDK estimator (kai, please confirm timeline)
- product to decide on opt-in server-side truncate (maria)

sam_support: will ping Acme now and include the KB snippet. also asked them for a small repro payload that hits 32k with only 1–2 docs (to see if any single doc is massive).

acme_dev: quick reply from customer: they suspect some legacy PDFs turned into huge HTML docs; will send one sample doc. thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:

maria_prod: noted — will discuss truncate option next AM with legal/privacy.

kai_engineer: I'll estimate effort: ~2 dev days to add token fields + SDK estimator, plus small docs update. will update INT-5234 with ETA.

jordan_support: thanks team — closing here once customer confirms mitigation works.


# end thread
